correctness.rationale: For q>=5, every torus evaluation section is A(x)+yB(x), deg A<=3, deg B<=1; evaluation is injective since q-1>3. One equation has at most 3t zeros. For two independent equations, gcd/factor classification of vertical factors and elimination A1B2-A2B1 (degree<=4) yields <=2t; witnesses are two vertical fibers. For three-dimensional systems, a common vertical x-r factor reduces to a three-dimensional subspace of span{1,x,x^2,y}, whose annihilator picks at most one off-fiber point; otherwise generic coprime pair implies <=4<=t+1. Four-dimensional common-zero points are on a projective line; three distinct torus points on a line necessarily share x, giving <=t. Five/six forms give <=1/0. Independently exhaustively checked all 2^16 torus point subsets at q=5 using exact modular Gaussian elimination: common-zero maxima (12,8,5,4,1,0). This is finite corroboration only.
